title: Synchronized arrivals at modest average load
question: Can finite buffering drop traffic even when average offered load is below capacity?
observation: The synchronized case loses half its offered packets under the stated FIFO model.
hypothesis: Instantaneous bursts, rather than the average rate alone, exceed the available capacity.
nextExperiment: Compare uniformly staggered arrivals with all other model settings fixed.
limits: Nearest-rank p99 covers accepted packets only; no hardware run.

title: Same load, different synchronization
question: What changes when the same senders start at different phases?
observation: Uniform phasing delivers all offered packets in the reference model.
hypothesis: Reducing coincident arrivals reduces queueing pressure without adding capacity.
nextExperiment: Hold phasing constant and shorten the sender interval to test sustained overload.
limits: Staggering is not a free optimization available to every real workload.

title: A larger buffer changes the question
question: Does eliminating drops also improve the delivered-packet tail?
observation: All packets are delivered, but the delivered-packet p99 increases.
hypothesis: A bigger buffer can retain packets that would otherwise disappear from the latency sample.
nextExperiment: Compare completion and loss alongside latency; do not rank cases by p99 alone.
limits: Capacity includes the packet being serviced, not just the waiting queue.

title: Phasing cannot create capacity
question: Can staggered senders overcome sustained overload?
observation: Loss persists in the sustained-overload reference case.
hypothesis: Phasing can reshape bursts but cannot change the server’s service-rate bound.
nextExperiment: Planned: test the model’s assumptions against a controlled hardware baseline.
limits: Synthetic FIFO outcome; not an NCCL completion estimate or a real GPU performance result.
